name: Segub
overview: Segub was a male figure in the Old Testament, known primarily as the youngest son of Hiel. His life is briefly noted in the context of his father's actions during the rebuilding of Jericho. Beyond this, Scripture provides no additional details about his tribe or other personal attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Segub means 'exalted' in the biblical record. This proper name is mentioned in 1 Kings 16:34 and was not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Segub is explicitly identified as the son of Hiel, as recorded in 1 Kings 16:34. No other family relationships are documented in Scripture beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Segub's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his death during the rebuilding of Jericho by his father, Hiel. This event is noted in 1 Kings 16:34, illustrating the fulfillment of a curse pronounced earlier in Israel's history regarding Jericho's reconstruction. Segub's mention underscores the serious consequences tied to disobedience and the fulfillment of divine judgment.
